proposed.text: Under BP 344 and its 2024 Revised IRR, what is the maximum gradient permitted for an accessible ramp serving a heritage building entrance (where no mechanical alternative is feasible)?

options.text: 1:8 - permissible only for very short ramps under 1.5 m
1:12 - the previous standard retained in the 2024 IRR for heritage retrofits
1:20 - the checked BP 344 2024 IRR maximum (1:15 allowed only in special cases for shorter runs)
1:25 - preferred for landscaped approaches but not the regulatory maximum

proposed.rationale: BP 344 2024 Revised IRR Appendix A.1.1 (Accessible Ramps) states verbatim that ramps 'shall have... Gradient not steeper than 1:20. Steeper gradients may be allowed in special cases depending on the length to be covered.' Table A.1.1 lists 1:20 as the standard maximum (15 m landing interval) and 1:15 only for special cases (max length 10.50 m, max rise 700 mm, 10 m landing interval). The older 1:12 value is not the current 2024 IRR maximum for general accessible ramps. Heritage status does not relax BP 344 ramp gradient; where strict application is impossible, RA 10066 / NBC variance procedure with a documented cultural constraint and an alternative accessible route is the source-safe path, not a steeper ramp.
